lesson_title: Five Boxes for Every Living Thing
hook_text: Every living thing on Earth, from your pet dog to the mould on old bread, fits into just five boxes.
clip_script: Scientists have named about two million kinds of living things, and South Africa alone has over twenty thousand kinds of flowering plants. To make sense of it, they sort. Box one: Bacteria, tiny cells with no nucleus. Box two: Protista, tiny cells with a nucleus, like the amoeba. Box three: Fungi, mushrooms, mould and yeast, never green, digesting their food from the outside. Box four: Plants, green and making their own food from sunlight. Box five: Animals, eating other living things and usually moving. Now the traps. A mushroom grows from the ground but it is not a plant. A whale lives in the sea but it is not a fish, it breathes air and feeds its babies milk. And a virus? Not even a cell. It does not fit in any box.
visual_style: Five whiteboard boxes filling up with quick sketches; a mushroom bouncing out of the plant box into the fungi box; a whale hopping from fish to mammals; a virus left outside.
pacing: Fast five-box fill, three quick trap reveals.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and sort anything alive into its box.
